$comment: The models a visitor may choose from, per role. THIS IS AN ALLOWLIST AND IT IS THE ONLY LIST THAT COUNTS. The browser sends a model id; the backend rejects anything not named here. Without that, a public URL is an invitation to spend the project's OpenRouter credit on the most expensive model available, seven calls at a time.
$verification: THE CATALOGUE FLAG IS NOT EVIDENCE. Every id below appears under openrouter.ai/models?supported_parameters=response_format, and two of them still fail in production: response_format support is per ENDPOINT, not per model, and require_parameters routes only to endpoints supporting everything sent. On 31.08.2026 gpt-5.6-luna returned OpenRouter 404 'no endpoints found' twice in one run, and solar-pro4 routed successfully and returned prose. The only verification that counts is a run. Every entry therefore carries an `observed` field saying what actually happened and when; add nothing here without one.
$price_note: price_per_m_in is dollars per million input tokens, converted from OpenRouter's raw per-token pricing.prompt (×1e6), checked 08.09.2026. It is one number for something that is not one number: gemini-3.6-flash alone quotes 0.375 on flex endpoints, 0.75 standard and 1.35 on priority. Price is per endpoint too, exactly as response_format support is. The figure here is the standard endpoint, and it is an order of magnitude, not an invoice.
$default_note: This is the fallback only. The committed per-role allocation lives in modelMap() in src/config.js and remains the artifact the model-progression argument rests on. A visitor's choice is an override on that default for one run; it is not the project's model decision.

$rejected.$comment: Candidates tried with `npm run try-model` and NOT added. Kept so the same model is not evaluated twice, and so the menu's shortness is a recorded result rather than an oversight. A rejection here is one observation, like an `observed` field, and is dated for the same reason: endpoints and capacity move. The rule for which list an id lands in is chronological, not qualitative: a model tested BEFORE being added and failing goes here, a model already in `models` that later fails keeps its entry and carries the failure in `observed` — so nothing that an archived run references is ever removed.
$rejected.deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash-0731: no answer within 120s — the call was cut off, not refused (31.08.2026). Two minutes is longer than any seat should wait; not a borderline case.
$rejected.inclusionai/ling-3.0-flash: returned JSON in 29s but omitted the required `reasoning` field, so G2 rejected it (31.08.2026). It can produce the shape and not the substance, which is the harder failure to notice.
$rejected.z-ai/glm-5.3-flash: no answer within 45s, and no answer within 120s on a second attempt (08.09.2026). Two cut-offs at two different bounds is not a slow model, it is an unreachable one.
$rejected.ibm-granite/granite-4.2-8b: returned valid JSON in 46.1s whose first `grounds` entry exceeded the schema's 400-character cap (08.09.2026). The only candidate so far to fail on length rather than on shape or silence — see the open question in docs/turns/018, because a bound tight enough to reject good output has been a bug in the bound before now.
$rejected.qwen/qwen3.8-flash: OpenRouter 429, 'temporarily rate-limited upstream', on two attempts four minutes apart (08.09.2026). This is a verdict on the provider's capacity today and not on the model; it is worth retrying if a seat is ever needed.
$rejected.dots-studio/dots-3-note-preview:free: no answer within 45s (08.09.2026). Not retried at 120s, because by then seven working models were already in hand — recorded as untested at the longer bound rather than as a failure at it.
$rejected.meta/muse-spark-1.3-contributor: OpenRouter 403 in 0.3s: the model requires an 18+ age confirmation on the account before use (08.09.2026). NOT A VERDICT ON THE MODEL — it was never called. Recorded so the next person does not spend a call rediscovering an account setting. Reachable if the confirmation is completed at openrouter.ai/settings/preferences.
$rejected.inclusionai/ling-3.0-flash-fin: returned an empty response in 13.6s (08.09.2026). The second inclusionAI model to fail this screen — `ling-3.0-flash` produced JSON missing `reasoning` on 31.08 — which is two observations of the same family failing in two different ways.
$rejected.liquid/lfm-2.5-2.6b:free: works — produced a valid judge opinion (not_justified) in 38.9s (08.09.2026) — and is rejected anyway. A test on this file has forbidden `:free` ids since turn 008, on the grounds that a free tier rate-limits, and adding this one made that test fail. The rule was right on the day: qwen3.8-flash returned OpenRouter 429 'temporarily rate-limited upstream' twice within the same hour. A seat that works in screening and 429s under a seven-call run is worse than no seat. This is the only entry in this file rejected for a reason other than what it did when called.

models.observed: works — the committed model for the first judge's seat, used in 19 recorded runs (31.08.2026)

models.label: Gemini 3.7 Flash
models.note: Same family, more capable. The natural first comparison.

models.label: Gemini 3.8 Flash
models.note: The newest of the Gemini flashes and the same price as 3.7. Added for decision 0013, which needs seven distinct models and takes the near-siblings on the advocate side where the seat already fixes what gets argued.
models.observed: works — produced a valid judge opinion (justified) in 26.8s (08.09.2026)

models.label: Gemini 3.6 Flash
models.note: The generation between the baseline and 3.7. Added for decision 0013. Its price varies more than any other entry here by endpoint — see $price_note.
models.observed: works — produced a valid judge opinion (not_justified) in 34.8s (08.09.2026)

models.label: Qwen 3.7 Flash
models.note: The cheapest credible option here, and it was reliable in screening. Held grey_worm's seat under decision 0013 and lost it on 08.09.2026.
models.observed: UNRELIABLE — argued the prosecution seat cleanly in screening (31.08.2026), then failed 3 of 5 production runs in an advocate's seat: OpenRouter 429 "temporarily rate-limited upstream" twice, and one call cut off at 90s (08.09.2026). The same upstream capacity problem that made qwen3.8-flash unusable a day earlier. Nothing wrong with the model; it cannot be counted on to answer.

models.label: Nemotron 3.5 Lightning
models.note: The first model on this list to earn its place before being added rather than after. Found by filtering openrouter.ai for cheap models supporting response_format, then verified with `npm run try-model` — one call, not seven.
models.observed: UNRELIABLE — passed screening in 14.4s (31.08.2026), then FAILED ALL FIVE production runs in shamgar's seat (08.09.2026): three on `/responds_to/0/answer must NOT have fewer than 20 characters`, one on a `representative_id` pattern, one cut off at 90s. It answers four advocates far more tersely than it answered the two the screening tool used to stub. One screening pass against five production failures is the clearest evidence this project has that a single call is not a verdict; the screen has been widened to four advocates and this entry is the reason.

models.label: Mercury 2.5 Preview
models.note: A fifth provider, and the fastest model measured for this project. One of eight candidates screened on 08.09.2026 and the only one of the first five to pass.
models.observed: works — produced a valid judge opinion (justified) in 6.2s (08.09.2026)

models.label: Seed 2.1 Turbo
models.note: A sixth provider. Offered but deliberately NOT allocated a seat in decision 0013: the advocates run concurrently, so the slowest advocate sets the length of the whole first stage, and a model with this spread would set it alone.
models.observed: works (slow) — produced a valid judge opinion (not_justified) in 99.6s, after two earlier attempts were cut off at 45s (08.09.2026). It answers; it cannot be relied on to answer promptly.

models.label: Muse Glimmer 30B
models.note: A seventh provider, and by some way the largest model on this list. Chosen for shamgar's seat on that basis: the seat's previous occupant failed by writing three-word answers under a 20-character floor, so size was the axis that mattered rather than price or speed.
models.observed: works — produced a valid judge opinion (not_justified) in 33.2s (08.09.2026), screened against four stub advocates rather than two

models.label: Mercury 2.5
models.note: The general-availability model behind mercury-2.5-preview, which sits on elon's seat. A DIFFERENT ID AND ARGUABLY NOT A DIFFERENT MODEL — see decision 0013's amendment, which says so rather than letting the allocation look more varied than it is.
models.observed: works — produced a valid judge opinion (not_justified) in 5.1s (08.09.2026), the fastest call this project has measured

models.label: GPT-5.6 Luna
models.note: A different provider, which is the point of having more than one. Price checked against openrouter.ai/openai/gpt-5.6-luna on 31.08.2026 and corrected from 0.10, which was wrong when it was written.
models.observed: FAILS — OpenRouter 404, "no endpoints found that can handle the requested parameters", on both roles that used it (31.08.2026). Listed in the response_format catalogue and still unroutable with require_parameters. Kept rather than removed so that archived runs which used it still resolve; no longer offered in the picker.
